findings.description: `server_name.partition(":")` splits on the first colon. For an IPv6 SERVER_NAME such as `[::1]:5000`, host becomes `[` and port becomes `:1]:5000`. Then `int(sn_port)` raises ValueError in `run()`, or the host is wrong. The previous `urlsplit` code handled bracketed IPv6 correctly and also validated the port.
findings.suggestion: Keep using `urlsplit(f"//{server_name}")` to get hostname and port, or parse bracketed hosts explicitly.
findings.title: SERVER_NAME parsing via partition breaks IPv6 literals

findings.description: `ctx.request.host.partition(":")[0]` splits on the first colon. For an IPv6 host like `[::1]:5000`, it yields `[`, so the cookie domain is wrong and session cookies are not matched on later requests. The old code used `urlsplit(...).hostname or "localhost"`, which handled IPv6 and gave a fallback for an empty host. An empty host now yields an empty string.
findings.title: Cookie domain derived by partition on host breaks IPv6 and drops localhost fallback
